subject.title: RFC: Readiness Providers and Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw own readiness providers and standard hosting profiles as durable core plugin, configuration, and release-support contracts?
rationale: The proposal is technically coherent but deliberately creates public API/configuration surface and a new operational support promise; automated review cannot choose that product boundary.

options.title: Review the full contract
options.body: Keep the draft open and evaluate the provider API, standard profile catalog, upgrade defaults, and release conformance as one coordinated direction.

options.title: Accept a narrower foundation
options.body: Advance only the canonical readiness-result layer and defer plugin providers, operator profiles, and the standard profile catalog to later decisions.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Keep hosting-profile composition downstream and close the RFC after recording the maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Review the full contract
recommendation.body: Keep the draft open and evaluate the provider API, standard profile catalog, upgrade defaults, and release conformance as one coordinated direction.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available product-routing signal is their documented review of the existing Gateway readiness and container support boundary that this RFC proposes to extend.
